headline: US GDP Grew at 4.3% Annual Rate in Third Quarter 2026
summary: The U.S. economy expanded at an annual rate of 4.3% in the third quarter of 2026, driven by increases in investment and consumer spending. This second estimate marks an upward revision from the initial 3.4% reading.
why: GDP is the primary indicator of economic health. An upward revision suggests stronger-than-expected momentum in the U.S. economy, which influences Federal Reserve policy and investor sentiment regarding growth assets.

impacts.name: S&P 500
impacts.why: Stronger GDP growth typically signals higher corporate earnings potential, supporting equity valuations.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: The upward revision to GDP growth indicates a more resilient economy than previously estimated, potentially supporting corporate earnings and investor risk appetite.
